we define two types of LEE-graph on the set of all the connected spanning k-edge graphs of a connected graph.

we give two approaches to the generalization of leaf edge exchange graphs on spanning trees to connected spanning k-edge graphs of a connected graph.

two kinds of LECs, which are defined on the set of all k-edges subgraphs of G, and show the existence of a transition sequence for the two kinds of LCEs.

the LEE-graphs on the set of all spanning k-edge subgrahs of G is connected for a 3-connected graph G.
the leaf edge exchange transition sequence is a connected graph on the set of all spanning k-edge subgraph of a graph for k >= 3.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the two kinds of LEO-graphs over the family of connected spanning k-edge spanning subgraphs of a 2-connected G, are connected and that the LEE-graph of the family of all spanning k-edge subgraph of a 2-edge-connected G is connected.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two different ways in which we can generalize the LEE-graphs on spanning trees to connected spanning k-edge graphs of a graph G.
the LEE transition sequence is a natural tool for the study of connected spanning subgraphs of a graph.
the transition sequence result of LEE on spanning trees can be generalized to connected spanning k-edge graphs of a 2-connected k-edge-connected graph.
